name: Word Clouds
description: Dozens of cut words packed into one silhouette — a lightbulb, a brain, an arrow — with a single word carrying the piece.
story: A word cloud works because it rewards two distances. From across a floor it is a shape: a bulb, a head, an upward arrow. From two metres it is language, and every word in it was chosen. Each letter is cut and mounted separately, so the wall shows through between them and the whole thing casts a shadow that changes as the day moves across the room. The hero word sits on deeper standoffs than the rest, which is what makes it read first.
bestFor: Reception walls, breakout areas and the end of a long corridor, where a piece has to work from thirty metres and from two.

name: Statement Walls
description: One line at monumental scale, cut and raised — the sentence a team reads on the way in every morning.
tagline: The sentence people read every morning
story: Most motivational wall art fails because it shouts. Cut lettering cannot shout; it can only be well made or badly made. These are single lines set at the scale of the wall, with the spacing and weight doing the work instead of exclamation. Several carry a motif alongside the words — a noughts-and-crosses grid broken by a winning line, that sort of thing — because a statement is more convincing with one small piece of wit next to it.
bestFor: Studios, classrooms, maker labs, startup floors and stairwells.

name: Line & Wire
description: Continuous outline pieces printed as a single filament line — bulbs on wires, each holding one word, in colour that is the material rather than paint.
tagline: Drawn in one line, printed in colour
story: These are drawn as outline and printed rather than cut: a continuous line of coloured filament, so the colour goes all the way through and there is nothing to chip or repaint. They are light enough to mount with tape alone, which makes them the right answer for a leased floor where drilling is not allowed. The row reads as hung rather than ruled — the drops alternate on purpose.
bestFor: Leased offices, co-working floors, classrooms and anywhere the walls have to go back as they were found.

name: Values Boards
description: A company's own words, composed as one group at varying scale — read as a set, not a list.
tagline: Your words, composed rather than listed
story: Every company has five words on a slide somewhere. On a wall they need composition, or they read as a bullet list that someone has enlarged. These are set at deliberately unequal sizes and alternating alignment so the group has a rhythm, with one word raised deeper than the others. The words are always yours; the composition is the part we do.
bestFor: Boardrooms, HR and onboarding areas, and the wall behind a reception desk.

name: Sacred Lines
description: Calligraphy cut as dimensional letterforms — a word, a name or a verse, raised off the wall and lit by the room.
tagline: Words with weight, cut and mounted
story: Calligraphy asks something unusual of a wall piece: it has to be beautiful before it is read and truthful once it is. Cut as dimensional letterforms, the stroke gains a real edge and a real shadow, which is closer to carved work than to print. Most pieces in the series can carry your own word, name or verse — in Urdu set in Nastaliq, in Arabic set in Naskh, or in Latin script.
bestFor: Entrances, prayer and quiet rooms, and offices that want meaning on the wall rather than decoration.

name: Brand Walls
description: Mark, wordmark and tagline cut in acrylic or brushed aluminium — the wall a visitor photographs before the meeting.
story: A reception wall does the same job as a business card and gets looked at a thousand times more often. Cut lettering is the only treatment that survives that scrutiny: a printed panel shows its edges within a year, and a vinyl wordmark shows them within a month. Brushed aluminium faces and matte acrylic are the two we recommend most, and both can be lit from behind where the wall allows it.
bestFor: Reception and lobby walls, meeting-room fronts, and any wall that appears in photographs of the company.

name: Mirror Acrylic
description: Mirror-faced acrylic in gold, silver or black — modular sets the buyer arranges, and single names cut in gold.
tagline: Cut in mirror, arranged by you
story: Mirror acrylic is the finish this market asks for by name, and it behaves unlike a painted face: it takes the colour of whatever is opposite it, so a set on a wall facing a window changes through the day and a set in a corridor stays quiet. Most of these are sold as sets of six to twenty-two components rather than one panel, which is the point — the arrangement is the customer's, and the gallery wall planner exists to settle it before anything is cut. Edges are flame-polished, because a mirror face with a saw-cut edge announces itself from across a room.
bestFor: Reception walls, restaurant and café features, hotel corridors, and any wall where the light changes through the day.
